what_its_for: Venlafaxine is used to treat depression, anxiety disorders, panic disorder, and social anxiety disorder. It helps balance certain chemicals in your brain (serotonin and norepinephrine) that affect your mood and feelings of well-being.
how_to_take: Take venlafaxine exactly as your doctor prescribed. Swallow the extended-release capsules whole — do not crush, chew, or break them. You may open the capsule and sprinkle the contents on a spoonful of applesauce, then swallow immediately without chewing. Always take it with food to help reduce stomach upset. Try to take it at the same time every day.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over time. A common starting dose is 37.5 mg to 75 mg once daily (extended-release) or in divided doses (immediate-release). Your doctor may increase your dose up to 225 mg per day or higher in some cases. Never change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store venlafaxine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store it in a dry place — avoid keeping it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking venlafaxine, as it can increase dizziness and drowsiness. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid stopping venlafaxine suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can cause withdrawal symptoms like dizziness, nausea, headache, and irritability. Avoid taking other medicines — including over-the-counter drugs and supplements like St. John's Wort — without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: thoughts of hurting yourself or suicide, new or worsening depression or anxiety, unusual changes in behavior or mood, seizures, fast or irregular heartbeat, severe headache, blurred vision, confusion, high fever with stiff muscles and sweating (signs of serotonin syndrome), unusual bleeding or bruising, or difficulty urinating. Contact your doctor if you notice significant increases in your blood pressure, as venlafaxine can raise blood pressure.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in sleep, appetite, or energy within the first 1 to 2 weeks. However, it usually takes 4 to 6 weeks to feel the full benefits for mood and anxiety. Be patient and keep taking your medicine even if you do not feel better right away. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor.
special_populations: Older adults (65+): You may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness and falls. Use caution when standing up quickly. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before taking this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Babies born to mothers taking venlafaxine near delivery may need extra monitoring. Breastfeeding: Small amounts pass into breast milk. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. Children and teenagers: This medicine is not approved for use in children, and young people may have an increased risk of suicidal thoughts especially at the start of treatment. Close monitoring is very important. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may need to lower your dose if you have kidney or liver disease.
